I have been farming this land for fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil — the Quzhou sandy loam, the well depth, how many irrigations wheat needs before the winter freeze. I do not read books or look at phones. I know what I know from doing it every year.

My body is not as strong as it was. There are only two of us — me and my wife. Cotton is hard work, especially the picking in August and September. My back hurts. But cotton still brings cash, and I have a small plot I have always kept. I will keep it small this year. Five mu of cotton is enough for two old people to manage. The rest — fifteen mu — I keep in my wheat-maize rotation like always.

For wheat, I will plant Jimai in October after the maize harvest. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at jointing. Four irrigations: before winter, at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain-filling if it is dry. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew in May. Rotary tillage before seeding, like always.

For maize, I direct-seed into the wheat stubble in June — no plowing needed, saves my back. I buy hybrid seed from the county supply shop, the same kind my neighbor uses. Two or three irrigations depending on rain. Spray once for corn borer, once more if there are armyworms — those have been bad the last few years.

For cotton, I plow deep in April. I plant Bt cotton seed — it kills most of the bollworm without as many sprays. Still, I apply pesticide four times. Cotton needs water, especially at boll-setting. My wife and I will pick it together in September.
